page.title: Best LDAC Earbuds Under $100 (2026): EarFun Air Pro 4 vs Soundcore, Nothing and CMF
page.desc: The EarFun Air Pro 4 is the best LDAC earbuds under $100: LDAC plus aptX Lossless, 11 hours per charge, multipoint, IPX5. Where the soundcore Liberty 4 NC, Space A40, Nothing Ear (a) and CMF Buds 2 Plus win instead.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best LDAC earbuds under $100 are the EarFun Air Pro 4 ({buy:earfun-air-pro-4}): LDAC plus aptX Lossless and aptX Adaptive, 11 hours per charge with noise cancelling off and 7.5 hours with it on, 52 hours with the case, IPX5, wireless charging and in-ear detection. The question most buyers ask is whether they can keep two-device multipoint while using LDAC. No. LDAC switches off two-device multipoint on every set here, and the Air Pro 4 is the only one that keeps multipoint on a hi-res codec, because aptX Adaptive and aptX Lossless stay on with two devices connected. Expect about 6 hours per charge with LDAC and adaptive ANC both on.

If noise cancelling matters more than codec choice, the soundcore Liberty 4 NC measured stronger in SoundGuys' lab (8.4 out of 10 against 7.5 for the Air Pro 4) and ran 9.85 hours with ANC on, but it lists at $99.99 on soundcore's store and has no aptX. The Air Pro 4 is the better buy for Android phones with Snapdragon Sound, and for anyone who wants LDAC, multipoint, IPX5 and wireless charging in one set under $80.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • LDAC or multipoint, not both. Four sources we read say it outright (Digital Trends and GamingTrend on the Air Pro 4, EarFun's own notes on the Air Pro 4i and Wave Pro). It is a Bluetooth bandwidth limit, not a defect. On the Air Pro 4, switch to aptX Adaptive if you need two devices.
  • LDAC stutter at 990 kbps. Five forum threads (a Pixel 9 Pro XL owner, two Head-Fi users, Sony and FiiO support threads) describe drops at the top bitrate, often with the phone screen on. SoundGuys saw the Nothing Ear (a) stutter in busy streets. Set LDAC to 660 kbps or adaptive in developer options and it usually stops.
  • One bud goes silent. EarFun's support forum has eight Air Pro 4 threads about a dead or unpaired left bud. Forgetting the pairing on the phone and re-pairing fixed most; the rest went to the 18-month warranty.
  • Touch mis-taps. SoundGuys hit single-tap volume while seating the buds; TechRadar noted a lag before taps register. Remap or disable single tap in the app.
  • iPhone gets AAC only. Three reviews point out that LDAC and aptX never engage on iOS. One pre-launch unit also had iOS dropouts and short range; later firmware addressed it.
  • Mics in noise. SoundGuys, Digital Trends and RTINGS all rate the EarFun mics average on a loud street.

Which one by need

  • Snapdragon Sound phone, or multipoint plus hi-res: EarFun Air Pro 4 ({buy:earfun-air-pro-4}). aptX Lossless on a supported phone, aptX Adaptive with two devices, LDAC when you want it.
  • Strongest ANC and longest ANC-on battery with LDAC: soundcore Liberty 4 NC (8.4 out of 10, 9.85 hours) or Space A40 (8.5, 8 hours). Both are LDAC-only and IPX4; the A40's mic is weaker and its fit less secure. Check soundcore's store and Amazon on the day, since both are usually well under list.
  • Smallest budget: CMF Buds 2 Plus at $59 on Nothing's US store, 14 hours per charge with ANC off and IP55, but no wireless charging and sold out there on 2026-11-06.
  • Design first: Nothing Ear (a) at $79, IP54, but 5.5 hours claimed with ANC on and the weakest measured ANC in this group.
  • Air Pro 4+ ({buy:earfun-air-pro-4-plus}) adds a balanced-armature tweeter, Bluetooth 6.0 and IP55, but RTINGS measured about 4.75 hours with ANC on. Buy it for the sound, not the battery.

Not recommended for this query

  • Sony WF-C710N and WF-C510: SBC and AAC only, no LDAC, despite the Sony name.
  • Sub-$50 LDAC earbuds: two reviewers note the audible gain from LDAC is minimal at that price; spend the money on ANC and fit instead.
  • Any LDAC set for an iPhone: the codec never engages, so judge on ANC, fit and mic quality.
sources: Digital Trends: EarFun Air Pro 4 review

notes: QUERY CHOICE: 'best LDAC earbuds under $100' (autocomplete-style phrasing; results today are scarbir's LDAC tag list and affiliate roundups, no measured head-to-head). The Air Pro 4 honestly wins the main segment on codec breadth (only sub-$100 set with LDAC + aptX Lossless/Adaptive), multipoint-with-hi-res, IPX5, wireless charging and in-ear detection, backed by Editors' Choice badges from Digital Trends (Aug 2024, says it beats the Liberty 4 NC) and SoundGuys (8.4/10, Dec 2024). Rival wins stated in the lead and table: Liberty 4 NC (ANC 8.4/10, 9.85 h ANC on) and Space A40 (8.5/10, 8 h) measure stronger on ANC and battery. PAIN POINTS (count of sources): LDAC disables multipoint 4 (Digital Trends, GamingTrend, EarFun 4i reviewer note, Wave Pro spec); LDAC 990 kbps stutter 5 forum threads + SoundGuys Ear (a); one bud dead/not pairing 8 EarFun community threads; touch mis-taps 2 (SoundGuys, TechRadar); iPhone AAC-only 3; mic average in noise 3; LDAC+ANC battery ~6 h 2 (Digital Trends, headphonecheck); 'LDAC gain minimal under $50' 2. SEGMENTS: Snapdragon/multipoint = Air Pro 4; ANC/battery = Liberty 4 NC (Space A40 close, weaker mic); cheapest = CMF Buds 2 Plus $59 (sold out at Nothing US today); design = Nothing Ear (a) $79. VERIFICATION: myearfun.com fails TLS for storecheck.py and WebFetch ('self signed certificate'); all store facts (prices, specs, policies, on-page codes DLAP4 and DLWP) were read today through the r.jina.ai text proxy of www.myearfun.com pages. Air Pro 4 $79.99 (list $89.99), Air Pro 4+ $99.99, Wave Pro $79.99 (list $99.99), all add-to-cart. US shipping free, 2-8 business days from a US warehouse. Warranty page says 18 months; a site banner says 'Lifetime Warranty', which the policy page does not back, so the records use 18 months. AMAZON: Air Pro 4 ASIN B0DM8R2M38 confirmed ('EarFun Air Pro 4 Adaptive Hybrid Noise Canceling Wireless Earbuds, 6 Mics', $71.99, 28,266 ratings) on 2026-11-06, i.e. $8 under the store today; the store's DLAP4/AMAP4 codes claim 36% off (about $57.59 if they work, untested). Kept the Awin record per brand mode; flag if you'd rather route to Amazon. Amazon then rate-limited amzcheck (blocked:true) so Space A40, Liberty 4 NC and Air Pro 4i ASINs could not be confirmed; those rivals are unlinked rows at soundcore's $99.99 list (verified via storecheck on us.soundcore.com today) with 'often discounted' wording (SoundGuys captures show $69.99 and $79.99 on Amazon, not verified today). Air Pro 4i: the store grid shows $59.99 but its product page exposed no price or spec table through the proxy, so no record was made (codes DLAP4I/AWAP4I25 therefore omitted). Codes for Clip, Clip 2, OpenJump, UBOOM L, Tune Pro, Wave Life, Air 2 NC omitted (no record); UK/EU-only codes (GSAP4P, GSWP41, GSAP439, GSA2NC58, DLEC) omitted. UNVERIFIED and kept off the page: Air Pro 4i specs, CMF Buds 2 Plus multipoint and ANC-on hours, RTINGS numeric scores (paywalled; only its text statements used), Reddit threads (blocked; one mirrored thread used for LDAC stutter). The SoundGuys 8 h 44 min Air Pro 4 figure does not state ANC on or off.
